title: Score Stick Scanner "pasha-ten"
description: Just snap a photo of the mahjong score sticks and AI counts them automatically. No more manual counting mistakes — easily record and share game results with friends and family.
overviewDesc: When everyone counts the score sticks by hand after a game, the totals often don't match up. To fix this small but frustrating problem, I built an app that reads the sticks straight from a photo using AI and tallies the score automatically. Friends and family can record and share scores together in a shared group (room), and each person can also see their overall results across every group they've played in.

highlights.title: Custom AI Model Running in the Browser
highlights.desc: Built a custom AI model (ONNX) trained on photos I collected myself to read stick counts and scores. The model runs entirely in the user's browser — no server inference — keeping operating costs at zero while returning results instantly.

highlights.title: Room-Based Score Sharing × Running Totals
highlights.desc: Organize friends and family into rooms to share game results. Players can view not just a single session's result but their cumulative score across every room they've participated in.

highlights.title: Serverless × IaC for Low-Cost Operations
highlights.desc: Infrastructure managed with AWS SAM (Lambda) + DynamoDB + Terraform. Achieves a scalable, serverless setup that minimizes ongoing maintenance costs.

timeline.desc: The project started from an everyday frustration: counting score sticks by hand often led to mismatched totals. I set out to build something that could read the score from a simple photo.

Using photos I collected myself, I built my own AI model (an ONNX file) that reads the number and value of score sticks from a photo. The model runs right in the user's browser instead of on a server, which keeps running costs down while still returning results instantly.
Built a way to organize friends and family into groups, so it's clear who played together in each session.
Game results are recorded automatically, and each player can check not just a single session's result but their running total across every game they've taken part in.
Reorganized the code by responsibility so it stays easy to read and easy to update going forward.
